PCR of the head fragment and of the stalk plus vector fragment should be performed following the manufacture’s instruction using Q5® High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase. We routinely perform minor changes, such as increasing the denaturation/annealing and extension times. In Table 1, Table 2, the thermocycler protocols used for amplification of the HA stalk plus vector and the HA head fragments are reported.

When the amplification of the target DNA has been confirmed, the PCR reaction must be purified before proceeding to additional steps (e.g. DpnI digestion or Gibson Assembly). QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (QIAGEN) or similar can be used for this purpose. DNA concentration should be measured using Nanodrop instruments or a spectrophotometer.

Colony PCR can be performed as follows.iA PCR stock mix can be prepared by considering the number of samples to be screened and for each reaction adding 12.5 μl of DreamTaq Green PCR Master Mix, 0.1 μl of each Fwd and Rev primers (final concentration 400 nM).iiSubsequently the PCR stock mix should be aliquoted into PCR microtubes (20 μl in each tube).iiiAlongside the PCR stock mix preparation, each bacterial colony to be tested should be numbered and diluted in 20 μl of DNase/RNase free water before streaking the colony onto a numbered grid previously prepared on an appropriate LB Agar plate.ivNegative (colony with empty vector) and positive (colony with vector and insert) controls are inserted if available.vAn additional control consisting of DNase/RNase free water can be added to evaluate if carry‐over of DNA was present during the procedure.viAfter a lysis step at 94 °C for 3 min in a thermal cycler, 5 μl of each colony suspension is transferred to a numbered PCR microtube in which 20 μl of PCR mix is already present.viiTubes should be positioned in a thermocycler and the colony PCR program detailed in Table 3 should be run.viiiAmplification of the target sequence should be verified through analytical DNA gel electrophoresis. If DreamTaq Green PCR Master Mix was used samples can be directly loaded on an agarose gel.

steps.title: Design primers using NEBuilder
steps.instruction: Generate the chimeric HA (cHA) sequence and design primers with the NEBuilder Assembly Tool.

substeps.instruction: Align the amino‑acid sequences of the two parental HAs using Jalview or equivalent software.

Identify Cys52 and Cys277 (H3 numbering) in each HA; verify that these residues correspond to the hinge cysteines by inspecting available crystal structures from the RCSB PDB (visualise with Swiss‑PDB‑Viewer, UCSF Chimera, RasMol, Jmol, etc.).
Assemble the predicted cHA amino‑acid sequence by removing the original HA head (between the two cysteines) and inserting the head sequence of the second HA.

Determine the nucleotide positions that encode Cys52 and Cys277 for the stalk HA (parental 2) using DNADynamo, BioEdit or similar; record the last nucleotide of Cys52 and the first nucleotide of Cys277.
For the head HA (parental 1), copy the nucleotide segment between the identified Cys52 and Cys277 positions into a new text file.
Open the NEBuilder Assembly Tool (http://nebuilder.neb.com/), set preferences to the E5510 Gibson Assembly Cloning kit, and select “Build Construct”.

Add the full nucleotide sequence of the stalk HA, name it “STALK”, and designate it as the vector backbone; choose “PCR” for linearisation and define the insert site by the previously recorded upstream and downstream flanking bases.
Add the head HA sequence, name it “HEAD”, and choose “PCR” for insert generation; keep all other parameters at their defaults.
Allow the tool to design forward and reverse primers and to suggest an annealing temperature; verify that the translated assembled sequence matches the predicted cHA amino‑acid sequence.
Order the primers from a commercial supplier, desalted and at 25 nmol scale or lower.

steps.title: Amplify fragments by Q5 PCR
steps.instruction: PCR‑amplify the stalk‑plus‑vector fragment and the head fragment using Q5® High‑Fidelity DNA Polymerase with extended denaturation, annealing and extension times.

substeps.instruction: Set up a PCR reaction for the stalk‑plus‑vector fragment according to the manufacturer’s protocol, using the thermocycler program reported in Table 1 (not reproduced here).
Set up a PCR reaction for the head fragment using the thermocycler program reported in Table 2.
After amplification, load 5 µl of each PCR reaction on a 0.7–1 % agarose gel to confirm product size.

steps.title: Run analytical agarose gel
steps.instruction: Separate the PCR products on a 0.7–1 % agarose gel; optionally run a preparative gel for band excision, in which case the subsequent purification steps are omitted.

steps.title: Purify PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify the confirmed PCR fragments using the QIAquick PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen) or an equivalent kit, then measure DNA concentration with a Nanodrop or other spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Perform Gibson assembly
steps.instruction: Assemble the purified stalk‑vector and head fragments in a 20 µl Gibson reaction and incubate before bacterial transformation.

substeps.instruction: In a 20 µl total volume combine 10 µl Gibson Assembly Master Mix (NEB), the purified stalk‑vector DNA and head DNA at a 1:3 molar ratio (e.g., 80 ng stalk‑vector ≈5.3 kb and 29 ng head ≈700 bp).
Add any required DNase/RNase as supplied with the master mix.
Incubate the assembly at 50 °C for 15 min.
Transform competent bacteria with the assembled product following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Optional colony PCR screening
steps.instruction: Screen multiple transformant colonies by colony PCR to identify those containing the correctly assembled cHA.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a PCR stock mix for the number of colonies to be screened: per reaction add 12.5 µl DreamTaq Green PCR Master Mix, 0.1 µl forward primer and 0.1 µl reverse primer (final 400 nM each).
Aliquot 20 µl of the mix into each PCR microtube.
Number each bacterial colony, resuspend each in 20 µl DNase/RNase‑free water, and streak the suspension onto a pre‑numbered grid on an LB‑agar plate.
Include a negative control (empty vector), a positive control (vector + insert), and a water control.
Lyse the colony suspensions by heating at 94 °C for 3 min in a thermal cycler.
Transfer 5 µl of each lysate into the corresponding PCR tube containing the master mix.
Run the colony PCR program as detailed in Table 3 (not reproduced).
Load the PCR products directly onto an agarose gel (DreamTaq Green allows direct loading) and visualise bands.
Select colonies showing the expected band (≈1.7 kb with vector‑specific primers or the size predicted for gene‑specific primers) for downstream plasmid isolation.

steps.title: Isolate plasmid DNA from positives
steps.instruction: Grow the selected colonies and extract plasmid DNA using the QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit (Qiagen) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Restriction analysis and Sanger sequencing
steps.instruction: Confirm the construct by restriction digestion and full‑length sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Use software such as DNADynamo to virtually digest the parental HA plasmids and the cHA construct, selecting one or two enzymes that give distinct band patterns.
Set up digestion reactions with FastDigest™ enzymes in FastDigest™ Green Buffer: 600 ng plasmid DNA, incubate 15 min at 37 °C.
Load the digested samples directly onto a 1 % agarose gel prepared with TAE buffer; include undigested parental plasmid as a control.
Visualise the gel with a gel‑doc system and identify clones displaying the cHA‑specific pattern.
Submit those clones for Sanger sequencing using primers that anneal upstream and downstream of the cHA insert.

steps.title: Confirm cHA amino‑acid sequence
steps.instruction: Compare the Sanger‑derived amino‑acid sequence of each clone to the theoretical cHA sequence generated by NEBuilder; note any point mutations introduced during PCR.
